record.context_brief: Power-Relaxed Greedy Algorithm in Hilbert spaces
record.original_question: Let H be a Hilbert space and D be a dictionary in H. For f in A_1(D), where A_1(D) is the closure in H of the finite expansions f = sum_{k in Lambda} a_k g_k with g_k in D and sum_{k in Lambda} |a_k| <= 1, consider the Power-Relaxed Greedy Algorithm defined by T_0^r(f)=0, T_1^r(f)=G_1(f), and for m >= 2 by T_m^r(f) = (1 - 1/m^alpha) T_{m-1}^r(f) + (1/m^alpha) g(R_{m-1}^r(f)), where g(R_{m-1}^r(f)) is a dictionary element maximizing the inner product with the current residual. Does there exist some exponent alpha_0 > 1 such that for every f in A_1(D) one has ||f - T_m^r(f)|| <= C m^{-alpha_0/2} for all m, i.e. a decay rate strictly better than the m^{-1/2} scale obtained from the known alpha = 1 result?

evidence.quote: Let H be a Hilbert space (over R) and D a dictionary in H. Related to this dictionary, we define A_tau(D), for tau > 0, as the clausure in H of the following set of functions: (f in H : f = sum_{k in Lambda} a_k g_k, g_k in D, |Lambda| < infinity and sum_{k in Lambda} |a_k|^tau <= 1).

Power-Relaxed Greedy Algorithm: define R_0^r(f) = R_0^r(f, D) := f and T_0^r(f) = T_0^r(f, D) := 0. For m = 1, we set T_1^r(f) = T_1^r(f, D) := G_1(f) and R_1^r(f) = R_1^r(f, D) := R_1(f). Then, for m >= 2, T_m^r(f) = T_m^r(f, D) := (1 - 1/m^alpha) T_{m-1}^r(f) + 1/m^alpha g(R_{m-1}^r(f)).
Question 1. Is it possible to find alpha_0 > 1 such that ||f - T_m^r(f)|| . 1/m^{alpha_0/2}, m = 1, 2, .. for every f in A_1(D)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a real Hilbert space and let D ⊂ H be a dictionary, i.e. a set of unit-norm elements whose closed linear span equals H. For τ > 0, define A_τ(D) to be the closure in H of the set of all finite linear combinations f = Σ_{k ∈ Λ} a_k g_k with g_k ∈ D, |Λ| < ∞, and Σ_{k ∈ Λ} |a_k|^τ ≤ 1.

For f ∈ H and h ∈ H, let g(h) ∈ D denote a dictionary element maximizing the inner product ⟨h, g⟩ over g ∈ D (assume such a maximizer exists). Fix a real parameter α > 0. The Power-Relaxed Greedy Algorithm (PRGA) is defined as follows. Set R_0^r(f) := f, T_0^r(f) := 0, T_1^r(f) := ⟨f, g(f)⟩ g(f), and R_1^r(f) := f − T_1^r(f). For m ≥ 2, define
   T_m^r(f) := (1 − 1/m^α) T_{m−1}^r(f) + (1/m^α) g(R_{m−1}^r(f)),
   R_m^r(f) := f − T_m^r(f).

When α = 1 it is known that for every f ∈ A_1(D) one has ||f − T_m^r(f)|| ≤ C m^{−1/2} for all m ≥ 1.

Question: Does there exist an exponent α_0 > 1 and a constant C > 0 such that for every dictionary D in every Hilbert space H and every f ∈ A_1(D), the iterates of PRGA with parameter α = α_0 satisfy
   ||f − T_m^r(f)|| ≤ C m^{−α_0/2}   for all m = 1, 2, 3, … ?
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent work resolves the question negatively: for any α > 1, the Power-Relaxed Greedy Algorithm fails to converge for some f ∈ A_1(D). Specifically, a counterexample is constructed in R^2 with the dictionary {±e_1, ±e_2} showing inf_m ||f − T_m^r(f)|| > 0, so no rate m^{−α_0/2} with α_0 > 1 can hold. Thus no such α_0 > 1 exists.

status_evidence.title: Convergence Analysis of Greedy Algorithms with Adaptive Relaxation in Hilbert Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Taking α>1 for the (PRGA), there exists an element f∈A_1(D) with D a particular dictionary of R^2 such that inf_m ||f − T_m^r(f)|| > 0.
status_evidence.claim: For α > 1 the PRGA does not converge for some f in A_1(D), so no rate m^{-α_0/2} with α_0 > 1 is possible.
